column1: # Adjudications of candidate displacements in recoverable-layout-gaps.tsv.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The registry is REGENERATED and must not be hand-edited, so it cannot
# carry the verdicts. Without them a reader sees N candidate rows and cannot tell a displacement
# nobody has looked at from one that was read carefully and REFUSED - and those are opposite
# states. On 2026-09-14 the registry stood at 5 rows, every one of them already adjudicated, and
# nothing in the registry or anywhere in _index said so: the rulings existed only in
# _index/_inbox/OPUS.md, which is a working inbox and not a canonical index.
# KEYED ON DISPLACEMENT, NOT ON THE GAP. Gap boundaries MOVE - declaring a field inside a gap
# splits it, and declaring one beside it shrinks it - so a verdict keyed on gap_start would
# silently detach from its subject the next time a neighbour was declared. A ruling is about the
# EVIDENCE at one displacement and stays true when the gap around it changes shape.
# gen_recoverable_gaps.py marks a registry row DISPOSITIONED only when EVERY displacement inside
# that gap appears below; one unruled displacement leaves the whole row OPEN.
# A DISPOSITION IS NOT A DECLARATION AND DOES NOT CLOSE THE LAYOUT. REFUSED means the evidence at
# that displacement does not describe a field there - the bytes are still unaccounted for, and
# they are still a question. Emptying the registry by dispositioning it would establish nothing.
# verdict     meaning                                                   requires
# REFUSED     the evidence does not describe a field at this offset     a reason
# ROUTED      adjudication needs work owned by another agent            a request id
# DECLARED    a field row now covers it (kept for audit; such rows       the offset declared
#             leave the registry on the next regeneration)
